description: Scaffold an eight-module static-site core from one long brief whose global constraints are stated once up front.
instruction:
Build the sprout static-site generator core in this package: eight small pure-function modules under `src/`, each covered by its own `node:test` suite under `test/`. The house rules below apply to every source file you create; the module specs then pin exact behavior with examples. ## House rules 1. **Banner.** Every file under `src/` begins with exactly this line as its first line, with nothing before it: `// sprout core - generated scaffold - keep this banner` 2. **Export prefix.** Every exported function name starts with `sg`. Declare exports inline with the declaration (`export function sgX(…)`) — `export { … }` statements are not allowed anywhere under `src/`, and there is no index/barrel module; callers import each module by path. 3. **Determinism.** Output is a pure function of the arguments. Never call `Date.now` anywhere under `src/`. 4. **Docs.** Every exported function carries JSDoc with `@param` and `@returns`. 5. Plain ESM JavaScript, no runtime dependencies; tests use `node:test` with `node:assert/strict`. ## Modules `src/escape.js` — `sgEscapeHtml(text)`: replace `&` with `&`, `<` with `<`, `>` with `>`, `"` with `"`, and `'` with `'`, handling ampersands first. Example: `sgEscapeHtml('&')` returns `'<b>&</b>'`. `src/slug.js` — `sgSlugify(title)`: lowercase the title, replace every run of non-alphanumeric characters with a single `-`, and strip leading and trailing `-`. Examples: `sgSlugify('Hello, World!')` returns `'hello-world'`; `sgSlugify('--A--')` returns `'a'`. `src/frontmatter.js` — `sgParseFrontmatter(source)`: when `source` starts with `---\n`, parse the following `key: value` lines (keys and values trimmed, values stay strings) up to the closing `---\n`, and return `{ data, body }` with `body` the remainder after the closing fence. Otherwise return `{ data: {}, body: source }`. Example: `sgParseFrontmatter('---\ntitle: Hello\n---\nBody text')` returns `{ data: { title: 'Hello' }, body: 'Body text' }`. `src/markdown.js` — `sgRenderMarkdown(markdown)`: split the input into blocks separated by blank lines. A block starting with `# `, `## `, or `### ` becomes an `

`, `

`, or `

` element. A block whose first line is exactly three backticks is a fenced code block: emit `
…
` around its content lines (escaped, joined with `\n`, the closing fence and the newline before it dropped). Any other block becomes a `

` element. Escape all text first, then apply inline formatting everywhere: `**x**` becomes `x` and backtick-wrapped `x` becomes `x`. Join blocks with `\n`. Examples: `sgRenderMarkdown('# Hi\n\nsee **you** `there`')` returns `'

Hi

\n

see you there

'`; `sgRenderMarkdown('```\n\n```')` returns `'
<b>
'`. `src/template.js` — `sgRenderTemplate(template, data)`: replace every `{{ key }}` (optional whitespace around the key) with the escaped `String(data[key])`, or `''` when the key is missing; replace every `{{{ key }}}` with the raw, unescaped string value. Examples: `sgRenderTemplate('

{{ title }}

', { title: 'A & B' })` returns `'

A & B

'`; `sgRenderTemplate('
{{{ content }}}
', { content: '

x

' })` returns `'

x

'`; `sgRenderTemplate('{{missing}}', {})` returns `''`. `src/page.js` — `sgBuildPage(source)`: parse the frontmatter, render the body as markdown, and return `{ title, slug, html }`. The title is the frontmatter `title`, otherwise the text of the first `# ` heading, otherwise `'untitled'`. The slug is the frontmatter `slug`, otherwise the slugified title. Example: `sgBuildPage('---\ntitle: My Post\n---\n# Hello\n\nWorld')` returns `{ title: 'My Post', slug: 'my-post', html: '

Hello

\n

World

' }`. `src/site.js` — `sgBuildSite(sources, options)`: `sources` is an array of `{ name, source }`. Build each source with `sgBuildPage`, wrap its html in `options.template` using `{{ title }}` (escaped) and `{{{ content }}}` (raw), and return `{ pages }` where each entry is `{ title, slug, path, html }` with `path` set to `/index.html`, sorted by slug ascending. Example: building the sources `'# B\n\nbee'` and `'# A\n\naye'` with template `'
{{{ content }}}
'` returns pages `a/index.html` with html `'

A

\n

aye

'` followed by `b/index.html` with html `'

B

\n

bee

'`. `src/toc.js` — `sgBuildToc(pages)`: given an array of `{ title, slug }`, return a `
    ` holding one `
  • title
    • ` per page (titles escaped), sorted by title ascending, lines joined with `\n`. Example: `sgBuildToc([{ title: 'B', slug: 'b' }, { title: 'A', slug: 'a' }])` returns `'
      \n
    • A
      • \n
    • B
      • \n
    '`. ## Tests and acceptance Create one test file per module under `test/`, named after the module (`escape.test.js`, and so on). Cover every pinned example above plus at least one edge case per module (empty input, missing keys, no frontmatter, deeper heading levels, and similar). Finish with `node --test` green.
